Rashi on Ketubot 12b:10:1.hebrew: אלא דאיכא מגו] - כגון משארסתני נאנסתי, וכגון היא אומרת מוכת עץ אני, דאמרינן מגו דאי בעיא טענה טענה מעלייתא מהך. כגון גבי משארסתני נאנסתי, הוה טענה מוכת עץ אני [טענה מעלייתא], דלא פסלה נפשה מכהונה, וקאמרה נאנסתי [משארסתני] וקא מיפסלה נפשה — דאשת ישראל שנאנסה אסורה לכהן — ש"מ קושטא קאמרה. וגבי היא אומרת מוכת עץ אני, אי בעיא אמרה מוכת עץ אני תחתיך ואית לה מאתן, וקא אמרה מוכת עץ אני קודם לכן ואין לי אלא מנה:
Rashi on Ketubot 12b:10:1.english: Only where there is a miggo - For example, [where she claims,] "After you betrothed me, I was raped," and for example, [where] she says, "I am injured by wood," where we say that since [miggo] if she had wanted, she could have made a better claim than this one. For example, regarding [the case of] "After you betrothed me, I was raped," she could have claimed "I am injured by wood" — [a better claim,] since she would not have disqualified herself from [marrying into] the priesthood — yet she says "I was raped [after you betrothed me]" and disqualifies herself — for the wife of an Israelite who was raped is forbidden to a priest — [so] learn from this that she is speaking the truth. And regarding [the case where] she says "I am injured by wood," if she had wanted, she could have said "I was injured by wood while under you [i.e., after betrothal]," and she would have [a ketubah of] two hundred [zuz], yet she says "I was injured by wood prior to that, and I have [a claim to] only one maneh."

Rashi on Ketubot 12b:10:2.hebrew: אבל הכא - גבי האי תובע, מאי מגו איכא דלהמניה? הלכך, אוקי ממונא בחזקת מריה:
Rashi on Ketubot 12b:10:2.english: However, here - With regard to this claimant, what miggo is there that we should believe him? Therefore, leave the money in the possession of its owner.

Rashi on Ketubot 12b:11:1.hebrew: אוקמה אחזקה - מספקא לן אשעת ארוסין, אי בתולה הואי ונשתעבד לה למאתים, אי בעולה הואי. העמד אשה על חזקתה, ובתולה נולדה, והך השתא הוא דאיתניסה אחר אירוסין:
Rashi on Ketubot 12b:11:1.english: Establish her on her presumptive status - We are in doubt regarding the time of betrothal whether she was a virgin, and he became obligated to her for two hundred [zuz], or whether she was a non-virgin. Establish the woman on her presumptive status — and she was born a virgin — and [say that] it is now, after betrothal, that she was violated.

Rashi on Ketubot 12b:11:2.hebrew: מאי חזקה אית ליה להאי - תובע, דנוקמיה אחזקיה לגבות? הלכך, זיל בתר חזקה דממונא:
Rashi on Ketubot 12b:11:2.english: What presumptive status does this [one] have - [i.e., the] plaintiff, that we should establish him on his presumptive status to collect? Therefore, follow the presumptive status of the money.

Rashi on Ketubot 12b:1:1.hebrew: דמזלזלי בהו - באלמנות, קלות בעיניהם להוציאן מפני שכתובתן מועטת. תקינו להו מאתן, דגנאי היה להן. ואע"פ שאלמנות ישראל נמי כתובתן מנה, מיהו כהנים חשיבי טפי, וגנאי להם גירושי בנותיהן יותר מישראל:
Rashi on Ketubot 12b:1:1.english: That they were demeaning them - [Referring] to the widows: it was easy in their eyes to divorce them because their ketubah [payment] was small. They instituted two hundred [dinars] for them, because it was a disgrace for them. And even though Israelite widows also have a ketubah of a maneh, nevertheless priests are more prominent, and the divorce of their daughters is a greater disgrace for them than for Israelites.

Rashi on Ketubot 12b:5:1.hebrew: נאמנת - קא סלקא דעתך משום דברי ושמא, ברי עדיף:
Rashi on Ketubot 12b:5:1.english: She is deemed credible - [The Gemara] initially assumes [that this is] because [in a dispute between] a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim], the certain [claim] is preferable.

Rashi on Ketubot 12b:5:2.english: This [woman] is in the presumptive status - that she engaged in intercourse before she was betrothed and misled him.

Rashi on Ketubot 12b:6:2.hebrew: פטור - מלשלם, ומכל מקום משבעינן ליה שבועת היסת, שכן הוא כדבריו שאינו יודע שהוא חייב לו:
Rashi on Ketubot 12b:6:2.english: Exempt - From paying; nevertheless, we administer to him a rabbinic oath [shevuat hesset] that it is indeed as he says, that he does not know that he owes him.

Rashi on Ketubot 12b:7:1.english: And he is a priest - That is to say, he is of valid lineage.

Rashi on Ketubot 12b:8:1.english: Even in the first - Regarding the claim of a ketubah.

Rashi on Ketubot 12b:8:2.hebrew: [אוקי כתובה אחזקתה — אחזקת הבעל. <abbr title="הכי נמי">ה"נ</abbr>, גבי מנה לי בידך איכא למימר נמי: אוקי ממונא בחזקת מריה, ופטור:
Rashi on Ketubot 12b:8:2.english: Establish the ketubah on its presumptive status — [that is,] in the possession of the husband. So too, regarding [a claim of] "I have a maneh in your hand," one can also say: Establish the money in the possession of its owner, and he is exempt.

Tosafot on Ketubot 12b:10:1.hebrew: אלא דאיכא מגו - האי שנויא לא אתיא אלא לרב נחמן, דלר' יוחנן בההיא דמוכת עץ ליכא מגו, כדמוכח לקמן. הקשה ה"ר יעקב מקורבי"ל: אכתי ע"כ הא דרב יהודה דשמואל היא, דאי לשמואל פטור, תקשי ליה ממתניתין דהשואל (ב"מ ד' צז. ושם:): "המשאיל אומר שאולה מתה והלה אומר איני יודע — חייב"; דלשמואל ליכא לשנויי כדמשני לרב נחמן ולרבי יוחנן, כגון שיש עסק שבועה ביניהן, ומתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם, דשמואל אית ליה בהדיא בפ' כל הנשבעין (שבועות ד' מז. ושם) דחזרה שבועה לסיני ולא משלם. וי"ל דאיכא למימר דלעולם "מנה לי בידך" והלה אומר "איני יודע" לשמואל פטור, ומוקי שמואל מתני' דהשואל כשיש עסק שבועה וכההוא תנא דאית ליה "מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם", והוא סבר כאידך תנא, דפלוגתא דתנאי היא בפרק כל הנשבעין (שם). [ועי' ביתר ביאור תוס' ב"מ צז: סד"ה רב הונא]:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12b:10:1.english: "Only because there is a miggo" - This resolution works only according to Rav Naḥman, for according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, in that [case] of a woman whose hymen was ruptured by wood there is no miggo, as is proven below. Rabbi Yaakov of Corbeil raised a difficulty: Still, perforce, this [ruling] of Rav Yehudah must be [in accordance with] Shmuel, for if according to Shmuel he is exempt, a difficulty would be raised against him from the Mishnah in [the chapter] HaSho'el (Bava Metzia 97a and there [97b]): "[If] the lender says: 'The borrowed [animal] died,' and the other says: 'I do not know' — he is liable"; for according to Shmuel it is impossible to answer as [the Gemara] answers for Rav Naḥman and Rabbi Yoḥanan — [namely,] in a case where there is an obligation of an oath between them, and since he is unable to take an oath, he must pay — because Shmuel explicitly holds in the chapter Kol HaNishba'in (Shevuot 47a and there) that the oath returns to Sinai and he does not pay. And one can answer that it is possible to say that in truth, [in a case of] "I have a maneh in your possession" and the other says "I do not know," according to Shmuel he is exempt; and Shmuel establishes the Mishnah of HaSho'el [as dealing with a case] where there is an obligation of an oath and in accordance with that tanna who holds "since he is unable to take an oath, he pays," whereas he [himself] holds like the other tanna, for it is a dispute of tannaim in the chapter Kol HaNishba'in (there). [And see with greater clarity Tosafot on Bava Metzia 97b, end of s.v. "Rav Huna".]

Tosafot on Ketubot 12b:1:1.hebrew: כיון דחזו דמזלזלי בהו - פירש בקונטרס שהיו קלות בעיניהן להוציאן, לפי שהיתה כתובתן מועטת. וקשה: דמעיקרא נמי הוו ידעי שקלות בעיניהן להוציאן, כיון דמנה חשיב דבר מועט. ונראה לר"י לפרש: "דמזלזלי בהו" — שמקצת בני אדם היו נמנעים מלנושאם, לפי שהיו קלות בעיניהן שאין לה כתובה אלא רביע ממה שיש לה לבתולה, ותקינו לה מאתן. כיון דחזו דפרשי מינייהו לגמרי, והיו קופצים קודם על בתולות ישראל ולא היה שום אדם קופץ עליהם — אהדרינהו למילתייהו. היינו דנקט מעיקרא "מזלזלי", שהיו נמנעים ולא לגמרי פורשים, ובתר הכי נקט "ופרשי":
Tosafot on Ketubot 12b:1:1.english: Once they saw that they were demeaning them - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that they were light [i.e., easy] in their eyes to divorce, because their marriage contract was small. And this is difficult: from the beginning as well they knew that they were light in their eyes to divorce, since a maneh is considered a small amount. And it appears to the Ri to explain "that they were demeaning them" — that some people were refraining from marrying them, because they were demeaned in their eyes since she only has a marriage contract of a quarter of what a virgin has, and [therefore] they instituted two hundred [zuz] for her. Once they saw that they were distancing themselves from them completely, and were jumping first to Israelite virgins and no one was jumping to [marry] them — they restored matters to their [original] status. This is why [the Gemara] initially used the term "mezalzeli" [demeaning], because they were refraining [from marrying them] and not completely distancing themselves, and afterward it used the term "u-farshi" [and they were distancing themselves]:

Tosafot on Ketubot 12b:5:1.hebrew: והוא אומר לא כי כו' - אע"ג דבסוף המניח (ב"ק דף לה: ושם) דייק מדקתני "לא כי" דמיירי בברי, הכא דליכא למיטעי קתני "לא כי", אע"ג דאיירי בשמא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12b:5:1.english: And he says: "Not so," etc. - Even though at the end of [chapter] HaMeniach (Bava Kamma 35b, and there) [the Gemara] infers from the fact that [the Mishnah] teaches "Not so" that it is dealing with a definite [claim], here, where there is no room to err, [the Mishnah] teaches "Not so" even though it is dealing with an uncertain [claim].

Tosafot on Ketubot 12b:6:1.hebrew: מנה לי בידך והלה אומר איני יודע - פי': "איני יודע אם הלויתני מעולם", אבל "הלויתני ואיני יודע אם פרעתיך" — תנן בהדיא בהגוזל בתרא (שם קיח.) דחייב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12b:6:1.english: "I have one hundred dinars in your possession, and the other says: I don't know" - Explanation: "I don't know if you ever lent me [anything]"; however, [if he says,] "You lent me, but I don't know if I repaid you" — we learned explicitly in [the chapter] HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 118a) that he is obligated [to pay].

Tosafot on Ketubot 12b:6:2.hebrew: רב הונא ורב יהודה אמרי חייב - לכאורה נראה דלית להו דרבי אבא, דאמר: מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם; דטעמיה דר' אבא משום דדריש (שבועות ד' מז.): "שבועת ה' תהיה בין שניהם" — ולא בין שני היורשין, כגון אמר: "מנה לאבא ביד אביך", ואמר: "חמשין ידענא וחמשין לא ידענא", ואבוה כה"ג, מתוך שאין יכול לישבע משלם. ואי "מנה לי בידך" והלה אומר "איני יודע" חייב, אין כאן שבועה, דאפי' הוא אומר "אין יודע" בכל — חייב! ותימה, דבפרק יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קלה. ושם) גבי האומר "זה אחי", משמע דאביי אית ליה: "מנה לי בידך" והלה אומר "איני יודע" — חייב, ובפ' חזקת הבתים (בבא בתרא לד. ושם) משמע דאית ליה לדר' אבא! וי"ל, דאפי' למ"ד חייב, איכא למידרש: "שבועת ה' תהיה בין שניהם" — ולא בין היורשין, דשניהם לא ידעי, אלא שעד אחד מעיד שאחד חייב לחבירו מנה, דבאבוה מתוך שאינו יכול לישבע משלם. תימה, דרב יהודה גופיה אית ליה בריש הפרה (ב"ק מו. ושם): אפילו ניזק אומר ברי ומזיק אומר שמא — המע"ה! ואין לומר דרב יהודה כסומכוס, דאמר ממון המוטל בספק חולקין ולא אזיל בתר חזקת ממון, ולהכי כי איכא ברי ושמא נוטל הכל, והתם דקאמר: "אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: זו דברי סומכוס, אבל חכמים אומרים: זה כלל גדול בדין כו'", אליבא דרבנן קאמר וליה לא סבירא ליה; דהתם (בב"ב דף צב:) משמע דסבר כרבנן גבי מוכר שור לחבירו ונמצא נגחן. ועוד, דתנן בפרק השואל (ב"מ צז. ושם): "המשאיל אומר שאולה מתה והלה אומר איני יודע — חייב", וקאמר בגמרא: "לימא תיהוי תיובתא דרב נחמן ור' יוחנן!" ומאי קושיא? הא ע"כ מתני' כסומכוס אפי' לרב יהודה, דלרבנן מודה רב יהודה דפטור, ורב נחמן ורבי יוחנן ע"כ כרבנן, דלסומכוס לכל הפחות חולקין! אבל אי פליגי אליבא דרבנן, ולסומכוס לעולם חולקין אפי' בברי ושמא, פריך שפיר ממתני' דכרבנן אתיא, דלסומכוס חולקין. וי"ל, דהתם ברי גרוע ושמא טוב, דלפי שהמזיק לא היה שם טוען זה ברי, ושמא דמזיק טוב, דלא הוה ליה למידע; אבל "מנה לי בידך", הברי טוב והשמא גרוע, דהוה ליה לידע אם חייב אם לאו. אבל קשה, דבעי למימר הכא הא דרב יהודה דשמואל היא, דפסק כרבן גמליאל, והתם ברי גרוע ושמא טוב, שהבעל אינו יודע מתי נבעלה; ואם כן, תיקשי דשמואל אדשמואל דפ' הפרה (ב"ק מו. ושם)! ויש לומר דה"מ למימר: "וליטעמיך". ועוד יש לומר, דסוגיא דהכא סברה ד"זה כלל גדול בדין" לא לניזק אומר ברי ומזיק אומר שמא, אלא כדקאמר התם: "אי נמי לכי הא". וקשה על זה, דאפילו לפי "אי נמי" דהתם לא אתי שפיר, דהא בסוף המניח (בבא קמא דף לה: ושם) אית להו לרבנן בהדיא דאפי' ניזק אומר ברי כו', ושמואל סובר כרבנן כדמוכח בהמוכר שור לחברו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 12b:6:2.english: Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda say [he is] obligated [to pay] - At first glance, it appears that they do not hold of [the ruling of] Rabbi Abba, who said: "Since he cannot swear, he must pay"; for Rabbi Abba's reason is because he expounds (Shevuot 47a): "An oath of the Lord shall be between the two of them" — and not between two heirs, such as where one said, "My father had a maneh in your father's possession," and [the other] said, "Fifty I know [about], and fifty I do not know [about]," whereas [with] his father [in] such a case, since he cannot swear, he must pay. Whereas if [in a case of] "I have a maneh in your possession" and the other says "I do not know" he is obligated [to pay], there is no oath here, for even if he says "I do not know" regarding the entire [claim], he is obligated [to pay]! And this is puzzling, for in the chapter Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 135a, and there), regarding one who says "This is my brother," it is implied that Abaye holds that [in a case of] "I have a maneh in your possession" and the other says "I do not know," he is obligated [to pay], while in the chapter Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 34a, and there), it is implied that [Abaye] holds of [the ruling of] Rabbi Abba! And one can say that even according to the one who says he is obligated [to pay], one can expound: "An oath of the Lord shall be between the two of them" — and not between the heirs, where both of them do not know, except that a single witness testifies that one [father] owes a maneh to his fellow, where regarding his father, since he cannot swear, he must pay. [It is also] puzzling, for Rav Yehuda himself holds at the beginning of [the chapter] HaParah (Bava Kamma 46a, and there) that even [when] the injured party says "certain" and the damager says "perhaps," the burden of proof is upon the claimant! And one cannot say that Rav Yehuda [holds] like Symmachus, who says that money whose ownership is in doubt is divided, and does not follow the presumption of possession, and therefore when there is a "certain" [claim] and an "uncertain" [claim], [the claimant] takes everything — and there [in Bava Kamma], where he says, "Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel: These are the words of Symmachus, but the Sages say: This is a great principle in law, etc.," he stated [that] according to the Sages, while he himself does not hold like them — for there (Bava Batra 92b) it is implied that [Rav Yehuda] holds like the Sages regarding one who sells an ox to his fellow and it is found to be a gorer. And furthermore, we learned in a Mishnah in the chapter HaSho'el (Bava Metzia 97a, and there): "The lender says: 'It died while borrowed,' and the other says: 'I do not know' — he is obligated [to pay]," and the Gemara says: "Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav Nachman and Rabbi Yochanan?!" Now what is the difficulty? Perforce the Mishnah is in accordance with Symmachus even according to Rav Yehuda, since according to the Sages Rav Yehuda agrees that he is exempt, whereas Rav Nachman and Rabbi Yochanan perforce [hold] like the Sages, for according to Symmachus at the very least they divide [the money]! However, if they disagree according to the Sages, and according to Symmachus they always divide even in [a case of] "certain" and "uncertain," [the Gemara] rightly challenges [Rav Nachman and Rabbi Yochanan] from the Mishnah, which follows the Sages, since according to Symmachus they would divide. And one can say that there [in Bava Kamma, it is a] weak "certain" [claim] and a strong "uncertain" [claim], for because the damager was not there, this one [the injured party] claims "certain," and the "uncertain" [claim] of the damager is strong, since he could not have known; whereas [in] "I have a maneh in your possession," the "certain" [claim] is strong and the "uncertain" [claim] is weak, since he ought to have known whether he owes [it] or not. However, it is difficult, for here [the Gemara] wants to say that this [ruling] of Rav Yehuda is [the view] of Shmuel, who ruled in accordance with Rabban Gamliel, yet there it is a weak "certain" [claim] and a strong "uncertain" [claim], since the husband does not know when she had relations; and if so, Shmuel's [statement here] would contradict Shmuel's [statement] in the chapter HaParah (Bava Kamma 46a, and there)! And one can say that [the Gemara] could have said: "And according to your reasoning!" And furthermore, one can say that the sugya here holds that "This is a great principle in law" does not [refer] to "the injured party says certain and the damager says perhaps," rather [it refers] to what [the Gemara] says there: "Alternatively, [it refers] to such a case as this." And there is a difficulty with this, for even according to the "alternatively" there, it does not work out well, since at the end of [the chapter] HaManiach (Bava Kamma 35b, and there), the Sages explicitly hold that even [when] the injured party says "certain," etc., and Shmuel holds like the Sages, as is proven in [the chapter] HaMocher Shor Lachavero.
